statusDefinitions.implemented: Present, production-reachable, and backed by named verification evidence.
statusDefinitions.partial: Present but has a documented boundary, structural risk, or incomplete verification.
statusDefinitions.planned: Desired in the target architecture but not implemented.
statusDefinitions.accepted_exception: A deliberate divergence from the target pattern with a recorded reason and guard.
statusDefinitions.deprecated: Present only for migration or compatibility and should lose callers.
statusDefinitions.unknown: Not yet reviewed with enough evidence to classify.

components.name: Excise.Core project
components.summary: Pure-.NET PDF object model, parsing, content semantics, editing, writing, security, and validation.
components.targetState: Remain UI- and platform-independent; expose explicit, bounded domain APIs consumed by every delivery surface.
knownGaps: The public library surface is intentionally broad and still needs periodic production-reachability triage.

components.name: PDF primitives and object graph
components.summary: Typed PDF objects, references, dictionaries, arrays, streams, strings, names, and numbers.
components.targetState: Keep primitives deterministic, allocation-conscious, and free of workflow or UI policy.

components.name: Parser, xref, filters, and hostile-input boundary
components.summary: Loads untrusted PDF bytes, recovers supported malformed structures, resolves xrefs, and decodes streams.
components.targetState: Every attacker-controlled size, nesting level, loop, and resource allocation is bounded and fails with a typed diagnostic.
knownGaps: Long-run resource budgets and reproducible minimized fuzz-corpus handling remain active work.

components.name: Document model and mutation boundary
components.summary: Owns PdfDocument/PdfPage state, page trees, annotations, forms, editing, merge/split, and high-level mutations.
components.targetState: Separate document lifetime, focused mutation services, and conservation policies so PdfDocument is not the accumulation point for unrelated workflows.
knownGaps: PdfDocument.cs remains a multi-thousand-line coordination surface and needs responsibility mapping before any split.

components.name: Content-stream walker and sinks
components.summary: One content-stream state machine tokenizes operators and emits shared glyph/state semantics to specialized sinks.
components.targetState: Keep one authoritative walk; new consumers add sinks or operator consumers and never duplicate PDF text/graphics state.
knownGaps: The renderer necessarily re-executes graphics/text state and is an explicitly tracked exception rather than a model for new consumers.

components.name: Font decoding, metrics, and subsetting
components.summary: Resolves embedded and standard fonts, CMaps, encodings, widths, Unicode mappings, and authored-font subsets.
components.targetState: One font interpretation contract supplies extraction, geometry, redaction, authoring, and rendering without duplicated width/encoding tables.
knownGaps: Full PDF font-model completeness remains broader than the currently supported corpus.

components.name: Text extraction, ordering, search geometry, and selection
components.summary: Turns walked glyphs into letters, words, reading order, search matches, and selection/copy semantics.
components.targetState: Share glyph decoding and geometry with redaction while keeping reading-order policy explicit and independently measured.
knownGaps: Extraction coverage remains a measured bound on text redaction completeness, not a proof of completeness.

components.name: Glyph-, image-, and carrier-level redaction
components.summary: Finds target glyphs/images, reconstructs content, scrubs non-page carriers, and reports removal outcomes.
components.targetState: Every shipping entry point uses the same fail-secure pipeline, and every security claim is judged by a non-Excise oracle or an explicit reason.
knownGaps: Three current redaction test methods are not independently corroborated and must be reviewed.

components.name: Fresh-write serialization and encryption preservation
components.summary: Serializes objects, content, xrefs, object streams, encryption dictionaries, and fresh rewritten output.
components.targetState: All mutations conserve unrelated document properties unless a named policy deliberately removes them; outputs remain interoperable with independent readers.

components.name: Encryption, permissions, signatures, and document validation
components.summary: Reads/writes encryption, interprets permissions, parses signature structures, and validates PDF/A and PDF/UA properties.
components.targetState: Security policy is explicit at action boundaries, cryptographic interop is independently checked, and validation claims name their external oracle where one exists.
knownGaps: Some permission enforcement and platform trust behavior lives at delivery-layer action boundaries by design.

components.name: Excise.Rendering project
components.summary: SkiaSharp rasterization of PDF operators, fonts, images, patterns, transparency, annotations, and forms.
components.targetState: Keep rendering isolated behind a stable API; split implementation by responsibility while preserving a single explicit render context and oracle-backed behavior.
knownGaps: Renderer partials remain several thousand lines each and re-execute graphics/text state as an accepted architectural exception.

components.name: Excise.Ocr.Native project
components.summary: Narrow native Tesseract C-API ownership, resolver, handles, and pixel/text marshalling.
components.targetState: Keep unsafe/native lifetime code isolated, source-generated where possible, and covered by platform-specific failure-path tests.

components.name: Excise.Ocr project
components.summary: Coordinates rasterization, OCR engines, confidence, layout, and searchable-PDF construction.
components.targetState: Remain an optional integration layer and stay off ordinary open/render paths until OCR is explicitly requested.

components.name: Excise.Avalonia project
components.summary: Reusable viewer control, continuous layout, input, selection, accessibility, and bitmap interop.
components.targetState: Own viewer interaction/render scheduling without duplicating desktop-app workflow or PDF-domain policy.
knownGaps: PdfViewerControl is still a large partial-class family whose ownership boundaries need measurement.

components.name: Excise.Cli project
components.summary: Command registration, argument/JSON contracts, batch workflows, and headless delivery of core operations.
components.targetState: Program is composition and dispatch only; each command delegates to a focused handler sharing the same workflow services as other delivery surfaces.
knownGaps: Program.cs remains a multi-thousand-line command host and needs command-boundary and duplication analysis before decomposition.

components.name: Excise.App project
components.summary: Desktop composition root, windows, view models, dialogs, workflow services, persistence, and platform activation.
components.targetState: Keep composition and user-facing policy here while moving each primary workflow behind a focused controller/view-model with explicit state ownership.
knownGaps: The main window view model remains the dominant state/orchestration hub.
Debug-only scripting and platform activation require conservative reachability seeds.

components.name: Main-window orchestration and feature state
components.summary: Coordinates document state and many feature workflows through one partial view-model family.
components.targetState: Become a thin workspace shell over separately testable document-session, navigation, redaction, editing, security, and background-workflow owners.
knownGaps: Large constructor/state surface and hand-built parameterless test composition couple otherwise separate features.

components.name: Repository verification system
components.summary: Tiered tests, fuzz/property checks, independent oracles, baselines, corpus contracts, and release evidence.
components.targetState: Every gate is deterministic, mutation-proven, non-vacuous, and names whether it is a correctness proof, a ratchet, or an advisory measurement.
knownGaps: The current t0 baseline reports an unwired-API key/baseline drift and three redaction methods without independent oracles.

components.name: Architecture registry, reachability, and derived diagrams
components.summary: Machine-readable desired/current architecture plus Roslyn and public-API reachability checks.
components.targetState: Registry data, actual project references, source/evidence paths, current/target diagrams, and issue-linked gaps are checked together in t0.
knownGaps: Symbol-level diagrams and responsibility metrics are not yet emitted by the Roslyn reachability tool.

relationships.rationale: Today the main view model directly coordinates redaction state; the target moves feature orchestration behind a focused workflow owner while keeping the core engine authoritative.
Rendering consumes parsed operators but re-executes graphics/text state because rendering requires canvas, font, clipping, pattern, and Type3 hooks the glyph walker does not expose.
Glyph removal must use the one authoritative content walk and reconstruction path.
Independent saved-byte, extractor, and renderer checks must corroborate each security-relevant redaction assertion or record a specific exemption.
PDF-domain behavior must remain usable from CLI, desktop, tests, and other consumers without a UI dependency.
Architecture data and diagrams are part of the same fail-on-drift verification system as tests and API reachability.

workflows.name: Open, parse, render, navigate, search, and select

steps.responsibility: Resolve the input, own document lifetime, and surface user-visible failures.
Parse untrusted bytes with bounded recovery and typed diagnostics.
Expose pages, resources, annotations, and document state.
Rasterize the requested page and overlays.
Schedule visible pages, input, selection, accessibility, and viewport state.
Produce search, reading order, and selection geometry.

workflows.name: Select or name content, redact it, scrub carriers, and save a safe copy

steps.responsibility: Collect user intent and page/document coordinates without owning removal semantics.
Locate text using the shared glyph/reading model and expose confidence limits.
Remove glyphs/images and scrub positionless carriers under explicit policy.
Write a fresh output while preserving encryption policy and eliminating prior revisions.
Corroborate saved bytes, independent extraction, and rendered ink for the relevant property.

workflows.name: Edit pages, annotations, forms, or authored content and save

steps.responsibility: Own transient UI state and confirm destructive or permission-sensitive actions.
Apply typed mutations with conservation boundaries.
Serialize the modified object graph and encryption policy.
Preview and independently comparable reopened output.
Rasterize pages at the OCR contract resolution.
Own native engine lifetime and marshalling.
Interpret OCR results and construct text-layer operations.
Persist the searchable result.

workflows.name: Inspect signature structure, integrity, and trust

steps.responsibility: Parse the signed object graph and byte ranges without trusting declared lengths.
Validate byte ranges, CMS integrity, permissions, and structural status.
Evaluate platform trust where available and present integrity separately from trust.
Cross-check representative signatures and malformed ranges with independent tools/fixtures.

concerns.name: Main-window state and workflow concentration
concerns.desiredState: The main window is a small workspace shell; feature state, cancellation, commands, and workflow policy have explicit owners and contract tests.
symptoms: MainWindowViewModel.cs is 3,729 lines before its additional partials.
The constructor accepts many services and also maintains a separate hand-built parameterless composition path.
Document, navigation, search, thumbnails, editing, redaction, security, and background work share mutable state.
rootCauseQuestions: Which state belongs to the document session, viewport, or a feature workflow?
Which partials communicate through shared fields rather than explicit contracts?
Which tests require the parameterless constructor because composition is not injectable?
Which extractions reduce coupling rather than merely move lines?

concerns.name: Outsized implementation units and responsibility accumulation
concerns.desiredState: Large files are justified by cohesive generated/table-driven behavior or decomposed along measured state/contract seams, with no duplicate engines introduced.
symptoms: Several production files exceed 2,000 lines, including renderer partials, the CLI host, ContentStreamWalker, PdfDocument, PdfViewerControl, and MainWindowViewModel.
Line count alone cannot distinguish irreducible PDF state machinery from mixed workflow ownership.
deterministicDiscovery: rg -n 'class |partial class |switch |case ' Excise.Rendering Excise.Cli Excise.Core/Document Excise.Avalonia/Controls
rootCauseQuestions: Is size caused by a cohesive state machine, unrelated responsibilities, duplicated policy, or generated/tabular data?
Which types have high fan-in/fan-out or share mutable state?
Would extraction create a second state machine or clarify an existing contract?
Which large test/tool files are off the shipping graph and therefore lower priority?

concerns.name: Architecture and security gate baseline is not green
concerns.desiredState: Every t0 architecture/security gate passes for reviewed reasons, and mutations prove each gate detects the defect class it claims to detect.
symptoms: The unwired-API gate reports 47 Excise.App.release entries that overlap the Excise.App baseline key.
Three redaction test methods have no independently detected oracle or declared reason.
rootCauseQuestions: Is the unwired delta a real Release-only reachability change, an assembly-key normalization defect, or stale triage?
For each redaction method, what exact property is asserted and which independent instrument can observe it?
Can the gate distinguish implementation gaps from checker false positives without blanket allowlisting?

concerns.name: Dependency advisory acquisition is not deterministic
concerns.desiredState: PR, scheduled, and release scans acquire current advisory data in a writable isolated cache, emit machine-readable evidence, and distinguish unavailable data from a clean result.
symptoms: dotnet list package --vulnerable reports NU1900 for App and App.Tests because the NuGet advisory cache cannot refresh.
The command still prints no vulnerable packages, which can be misread as a complete clean audit.
rootCauseQuestions: Why is only part of the restore graph attempting a denied cache write?
Which cache/environment contract works both in sandboxed development and CI?
Should advisory acquisition failure be a separate hard-fail status from vulnerable/clean?
How does this work align with the broader supply-chain epic without putting network checks in t0?

concerns.name: .NET analyzer, warning, and suppression policy
concerns.desiredState: One central policy enables an agreed analyzer level; new warnings fail in scoped projects; suppressions are narrow, justified, and verified on all target platforms.
symptoms: There is no central Directory.Build.props analysis policy.
CA1416 is suppressed across the entire desktop project.
The current build can succeed with NU1900 warnings despite documentation expecting a clean build.
rootCauseQuestions: Which warnings are product defects, cross-platform false positives, third-party rollups, or environment failures?
Which projects can enforce warnings first without forcing blanket suppressions?
Can CA1416 be replaced by platform guards and source-level suppressions?
Which analyzer findings overlap reachability and should share one root-cause issue?

concerns.name: Narrative architecture status can drift from implementation
concerns.desiredState: Current/target component status, dependencies, workflow ownership, verification, and known gaps live in the checked JSON registry; narrative docs explain concepts and link to it.
symptoms: Architecture, design, implementation-plan, and status claims are spread across documents and registries with overlapping authority.
Static diagrams and prose do not fail when project dependencies or evidence paths change.
rootCauseQuestions: Which claims belong in timeless narrative versus status-bearing registry data?
Which component boundaries can be verified from project references, paths, and reachability?
Which target relationships need an issue before they can be marked planned?
What diagram granularity remains readable and decision-useful?

concerns.name: Source provenance and independent-implementation assurance
concerns.desiredState: Every current source and vendored-data family has evidence-backed lineage, attribution, and a reviewed retain-or-replace decision without overstating clean-room status.
symptoms: Legacy v1 directly used PdfPig, PDFsharp, and PDFtoImage while the current stack removed those packages.
Historical planning proposed borrowing several implementation families, so package removal alone does not prove clean-room provenance.
The Avalonia dispatcher scheduler explicitly records an adapted third-party lineage.
deterministicDiscovery: rg -n -i 'adapted|vendored|derived|PdfPig|PDFsharp|PDFtoImage|ReactiveUI' Excise.Core Excise.Rendering Excise.App docs LICENSES.md
rootCauseQuestions: Which files are specification-derived facts versus copyrightable implementation expression?
Which current code descends from earlier Excise implementations that used external libraries?
Which adapted code should be retained with attribution versus independently replaced?
How should new vendoring or material clone introduction fail deterministically?

architectureRules.statement: Excise.Core must not depend on Avalonia, SkiaSharp UI controls, delivery projects, or platform services.
New extraction, geometry, or redaction consumers use ContentStreamWalker semantics rather than implementing another PDF text-state parser.
A security-relevant redaction assertion uses a non-Excise oracle or carries a reviewed method-level reason.
Desktop, CLI, batch, and library entry points delegate to the same core mutation/security semantics rather than copy workflow policy.
Registry IDs, paths, project dependencies, workflow references, and current/target diagrams are validated and regenerated deterministically.
